CLI tools are Rust's home turf: a single static binary, no runtime, startup in microseconds, and a dependency ecosystem built for exactly this.

The stack

Crate Role
clap argument parsing, help, completions
anyhow error reporting at the top level
indicatif progress bars
console colours, terminal width, spinners
assert_cmd + predicates end-to-end CLI testing
tempfile isolated test directories

Full example: a file search tool

Note the exit codes: 0 found, 1 not found, 2 error. That is the convention every shell script and CI system expects, and getting it wrong breaks pipelines silently.

Shell completions

Progress and output

Gotcha: write progress to stderr and data to stdout. Otherwise mytool > out.json fills the file with progress bar escape codes.

Detect whether colour is appropriate:

Respect the NO_COLOR convention — it is a real standard and users expect it.

Signal handling and clean shutdown

For long-running work, write output atomically: write to out.tmp then fs::rename — a rename is atomic on POSIX, so a Ctrl-C never leaves a half-written file.

Testing a CLI

assert_cmd runs the real binary — the only way to test exit codes, stdout and stderr together.

Exercises

  1. Build the findstr tool above and add a --count flag that prints only the number of matches.
  2. Add --json output that emits one array instead of JSONL. Which is better for jq? For streaming?
  3. Make it respect .gitignore using the ignore crate (the one ripgrep uses).
  4. Add a progress bar on stderr and verify mytool > out.txt produces clean output.
  5. Add a --exclude glob flag and tests for it with assert_cmd.
  6. Add Ctrl-C handling that leaves no partial output file.
